subject: AisleTwo: Regional fallback & customer ops checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: ops@aisletwo.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AisleTwo: Regional fallback & customer ops checklist

Hi Sara / AisleTwo ops team,

We’re seeing a regional control-plane/egress degradation at one of the primary cloud providers that is impacting token-serving and some model-serving tails for EU and parts of US ingress. Your traffic that normally routes through eu-central-1 is showing error rates and elevated latency; we’ve observed higher 5xx spikes and stalled prefix cache refreshes. Impact window started ~2027-04-03T08:40Z.

Immediate mitigation we can offer (lowest lift to your engineering team):

1) Use regional endpoint alias (recommended):
   - US: https://api.redwood.com/us-west-2/v1/generate
   - EU fallback (if eu-primary is degraded): https://api.redwood.com/eu-west-1/v1/generate
   Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" "https://api.redwood.com/us-west-2/v1/generate" -d '{ "input": "..." }'

2) Header-based soft-reroute (no DNS change): add header "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us" to prefer US-serving variants and avoid the impacted EU control plane path.

3) Short-term client-side tuning: increase retry backoff to 2.5s with exponential jitter and extend request timeout by +1.5x for streaming calls.

We’ve attached an outage diagram and collected prefix/cache logs for your team to correlate (outage-diagram.png, prefix-cache-logs-20270403.tar.gz).

Internal contacts I’ve CC’d will coordinate region-level routing and status updates. Please reply with which mitigation you can apply now and any blockers (e.g., DNS TTL, corporate proxy, S3 access for artifacts).

- Aditya Rao
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0122

From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@aisletwo.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:30:14 -0700
Subject: Re: AisleTwo: Regional fallback & customer ops checklist

Thanks Aditya — confirming we received this. Quick questions:

- If we switch to the us-west-2 endpoint, will we need to do anything about S3-backed assets that are stored in eu-central-1?
- Our DNS TTL is 300s; is a DNS swap required or is the header sufficient for most requests?

We’ll try the header approach first; can one of your engineers stay on Slack for coordination? I’ll loop in our infra lead if we need to change storage routes.

- Sara
Director of Platform Ops, AisleTwo
[support ticket: #8421]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@aisletwo.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:46:07 -0700
Subject: Internal: customer guidance + ops checklist (AisleTwo)

Folks — filing a short checklist we should push to AisleTwo and use for other customers until the provider stabilizes. Paste this to the status update and to the HubSpot incident:

Customer ops checklist (deliverable for 1–2 hour mitigation window):

- Owner assignments:
  * Primary customer contact: Aditya Rao (account lead)
  * Incident engineering owner (routing/fallback): Jonas Weber
  * Customer success/comm: Lauren Bishop
  * SRE escalation point (cloud provider): Neha Kapoor

- Immediate customer instructions (share as single-step guide):
  1) Prefer-region header (no DNS change): add header "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us" to all API calls. This will prefer our US serving fleet and bypass the EU control plane path.
  2) If you cannot add headers, switch to the regional alias endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/us-west-2/v1/. Note: update auth token host if you pin hostnames.
  3) If you rely on EU S3 assets, use signed URLs (they will continue to work cross-region). For heavy asset traffic consider pre-warming a short-lived replication to us-west-2; we can assist with signed copy scripts.
  4) For streaming sessions: increase client timeout to 30s and use 5s retry base with exponential backoff.
  5) If you operate behind a corporate proxy, check that the proxy allows the us-west-2 host; otherwise we can provision a temporary egress route.

- Internal actions:
  * Jonas: apply temporary canary routing rule to prefer US for AisleTwo (will not affect other customers).
  * Neha: open escalation with provider (ticket #PR-20270403-11) and push for control-plane recovery ETA.
  * Lauren: update status page + HubSpot record (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/aisletwo).
  * Aditya: coordinate on Slack and confirm AisleTwo has the header/alias applied.

- Communications to include in customer message: summary, expected impact window, checklist above, attachments (routing-playbook_v2.pdf) and a link to our live triage doc (Drive). Keep the message short and prescriptive.

I’ve attached the routing-playbook_v2.pdf with curl examples, header samples, and a tiny script to swap endpoints for node/python clients.

- Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[attachment: routing-playbook_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ops@aisletwo.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident next steps and draft postmortem link

Team — good job moving customers to the header-based fallback; AisleTwo reports degraded requests are down ~92% since we applied the canary routing and they confirmed header adoption.

Action items for post-incident:
- Jonas: include exact config changes (canary rule ids, timestamped) in the postmortem.
- Neha: paste provider support ticket updates and the final root-cause communication.
- Aditya/Lauren: schedule a 30-minute review with AisleTwo for Wed 2027-04-07 to walk through the incident and confirm any follow-up support (replication for assets / runbook handoff).

Postmortem draft (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abcd1234-outage-collab/postmortem-aisletwo-20270403.md

We should offer AisleTwo a one-week free Dedicated cache-provision (discount offer) only if they request it; wait for legal/pricing sign-off before committing publicly.

Closing notes: capture a small eval to track quality regression before/after routing change — we will attach that to the postmortem.

- Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
